key_insight: Dense Fe-based amorphous coatings resist long-term corrosion better, while increasing humidity reduces their friction coefficient and wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce low-defect protective coatings on Q235 carbon steel, with wear performance dependent on service humidity.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Assess droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and long-term corrosion behavior.
Test friction and wear against Si3N4 balls under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links higher porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficients and wear rates as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance ranges, and the humidity-dependent wear findings may not generalize beyond the tested Si3N4 counterface.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
